taxastand

The goal of taxastand is to standardize species names from different sources, a common task in biology.

Very often different biologists use different synonyms to refer to the same species. If we want to join data from different sources, their taxonomic names must be standardized first. This is what taxastand seeks to do in a reproducible and efficient manner.

taxastand parses each name into its parts (genus, epithet, infraspecific rank, author and so on), matches them to a reference taxonomy that you choose while allowing for spelling differences in the epithet and author, and resolves synonyms to their accepted names.

Installation

taxastand can be installed from r-universe or github.

install.packages("taxastand", repos = 'https://joelnitta.r-universe.dev')

OR

# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("joelnitta/taxastand")

Some of the sources of ts_load_ref() are Parquet files, which need the nanoparquet or duckdb package. Neither is installed with taxastand; it will let you know if one is needed.

Taxonomic standard

taxastand is based on matching names to a single taxonomic standard, that is, a database of accepted names and synonyms. As long as a single taxonomic standard is used, we can confidently resolve names from disparate sources.

The taxonomic standard must conform to Darwin Core standards and is supplied by the user as a dataframe (if your dataframe doesn’t use the exact same column names as Darwin Core, taxastand is flexible). ts_load_ref() downloads and formats several widely used reference databases, including World Flora Online, the Pteridophyte Phylogeny Group classification, ITIS, Catalogue of Life and the GBIF backbone. It can also read your own file or URL, and ts_subset_ref() keeps just one family or other group of a large source. See vignette("setup-reference") for details, including how to use tables from other packages such as taxadb.

library(taxastand)

ts_show_ref_sources()
ref <- ts_load_ref(source = "ppg")

Downloads happen only when ts_load_ref() is called, and go to a temporary folder unless you set cache_dir.

Example

Here is an example of fuzzy matching followed by resolution of synonyms using the dataset included with the package.

library(taxastand)

# Load example reference taxonomy in Darwin Core format
data(filmy_taxonomy)

# Take a look at the columns used by taxastand
head(filmy_taxonomy[c(
  "taxonID", "acceptedNameUsageID", "taxonomicStatus", "scientificName"
)])
#>    taxonID acceptedNameUsageID taxonomicStatus
#> 1 54115096                  NA   accepted name
#> 2 54133783            54115097         synonym
#> 3 54115097                  NA   accepted name
#> 4 54133784            54115098         synonym
#> 5 54115098                  NA   accepted name
#> 6 54133785            54115099         synonym
#>                              scientificName
#> 1             Cephalomanes atrovirens Presl
#> 2                Trichomanes crassum Copel.
#> 3 Cephalomanes crassum (Copel.) M. G. Price
#> 4           Trichomanes densinervium Copel.
#> 5 Cephalomanes densinervium (Copel.) Copel.
#> 6         Trichomanes infundibulare Alderw.

# Names to resolve: an exact match, a match that differs in the author's
# abbreviation, and an outdated name with a misspelled epithet
queries <- c(
  "Hymenophyllum wilsonii Hook.",
  "Crepidomanes minutum (Blume) K.Iwats.",
  "Gonocormus minutum"
)

res <- ts_resolve_names(queries, filmy_taxonomy)
res[c("query", "resolved_name", "matched_status", "match_type")]
#>                                   query                        resolved_name
#> 1          Hymenophyllum wilsonii Hook.         Hymenophyllum wilsonii Hook.
#> 2 Crepidomanes minutum (Blume) K.Iwats. Crepidomanes minutum (Bl.) K. Iwats.
#> 3                    Gonocormus minutum Crepidomanes minutum (Bl.) K. Iwats.
#>   matched_status       match_type
#> 1  accepted name            exact
#> 2  accepted name     auto_basexin
#> 3        synonym auto_fuzzy_canon

resolved_name is the accepted name for each query, and match_type says how it was found (exact, or one of the auto_* types for matches that needed some tolerance; see ?ts_match_names). The resolved_name column can be used for downstream analyses joining on other datasets that have been resolved to the same reference taxonomy.

Similar work

  • taxon-tools is a command-line interface program that was the inspiration for taxastand. taxastand originally required it as a dependency (removed in v2.0) and was a faithful port of its algorithms, but taxastand is now developed independently.

  • taxize is the “granddaddy” of taxonomy packages in R. It can search around 20 different taxonomic databases for names and retrieve taxonomic information.

  • TNRS, the Taxonomic Name Resolution Service, is a web application that resolves taxonomic names of plants against several databases.

  • taxizedb downloads taxonomic databases and provides tools to interface with them through SQL.

  • taxadb also downloads and searches taxonomic databases. It can interface with them either through SQL or in-memory in R.

  • taxonstand has a very similar goal to taxastand, but only uses The Plant List (TPL) as its taxonomic standard and does not allow the user to provide their own. Note that TPL is no longer being updated as of 2013, and its website is no longer online (linked above via the Wayback Machine).

  • taxify, WorldFlora and U.Taxonstand also match names in R against a reference taxonomy. The Benchmarks article compares them with taxastand.

  • rOpenSci has a task view summarizing many tools available for taxonomy.

Motivation

Although existing web-based solutions for taxonomic name resolution are very useful, they may not be ideal for all situations: the choice of reference database to use for standardization is limited, they may not be able to handle very large queries, and the user has no guarantee that the same input will yield the same output at a later date due to changes in the remote database.

Furthermore, matching of taxonomic names is not straightforward, since they are complex data structures including multiple components (e.g., genus, specific epithet, basionym author, combination author, etc). Several of the tools mentioned above match names fuzzily, but they differ in whether they take the author into account and whether the user can choose and version the reference database; the Benchmarks article compares them.

The motivation for taxastand is to provide greater flexibility and reproducibility by allowing for complete version control of the code and database used for name resolution, while implementing fuzzy matching of parsed taxonomic names.

Contributing

Contributions are welcome! Please see the contributing guide for how to file issues, submit pull requests, and run checks locally.

Please note that this package is released with a Contributor Code of Conduct. By contributing to this project, you agree to abide by its terms.

Citing this package

If you use this package, please cite it. citation("taxastand") gives the reference, for example:

Nitta, JH (2026) taxastand: Taxonomic Name Standardization. https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.5726390

The example DOI above is for the overall package.

Please also cite the reference taxonomy you matched against. For sources loaded with ts_load_ref(), see ts_show_ref_sources() or the ts_source attribute of the result.

Here is the latest DOI, which you should use if you are using the latest version of the package:

You can find DOIs for older versions by viewing the “Releases” menu on the right.
